A search method that matches meaning rather than exact words.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and time limit
sections.what: Sets the Node.js runtime and allows 30 seconds for the request.
sections.why: Keeps the request from running too long.

sections.name: POST (part 1)
sections.title: Search for company context
sections.what: Reads the company name and key, runs two web searches, and gathers text snippets with their sources.
sections.why: Gives the writing tools real, sourced details.
sections.watch_out: Only the first two of the three planned queries run, because of the slice call.

sections.name: POST: if
sections.title: Return the research
sections.what: Returns an empty result if nothing was found, or up to four snippets joined into one text.
sections.why: Keeps the caller from getting junk output.
sections.watch_out: An empty result looks the same whether the key is missing or no results were found, so the user cannot tell why.

summary: Searches the web for recent news and challenges about a company, if an Exa key is provided, to give context for writing.
purpose: Gives the writing tools real, sourced context about a company.
why: Likely reason: writing that refers to real company events feels more specific.
how: Runs two Exa searches, gathers short text snippets with their sources, and returns up to four of them joined together. Returns empty text if there are no results or no key.
inputs: Company name, role, optional sector, and an optional Exa key.
outputs: Research text, or an error with status 400 or 500.
risks: Failed searches are skipped silently. Results may be old, or about a different company with the same name.
debug: Empty research: check the Exa key and the search response. If results look wrong, check the company name used in the search.
